epic.intent:
Prove the planning and execution contract works from a second MCP agent host, a different host from the one that planned the epic.

Split out of "Cross-host validation and release" on 2026-10-03, where it was DM-13 (formerly board ticket 014.4). That epic closed with the packaged-build verification (DM-12) only; this part was not done.

successCriteria.text: A second MCP host completes a sprint through MCP using the same saved plan, without changing any stored ticket requirements.

epic.title: Second-host MCP validation

bundle.rationale: One sprint, one ticket: verification work with no code expected. The packaged builds it depends on were verified in "Cross-host validation and release" (DM-12).

exitCriteria.text: A second host completed a sprint on the same plan, with its run events attached.

sprints.goal: A second agent host runs a sprint on a saved plan through the packaged MCP entry.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A second MCP host completes a sprint through MCP using the same saved plan.
The saved plan revision and ticket capability requirements are unchanged before and after the run.
Run events and the sprint report from the second host are attached.

tickets.body:
Formerly DM-13 in "Cross-host validation and release" (board ticket 014.4). Run the same planning and execution contract from a second MCP host, a different agent host from the one that planned the epic, without changing the stored ticket requirements.

Use a small saved epic in a scratch repository. Connect the second host with the packaged app's MCP entry, run one sprint as orchestrator (claim, submit, accept), and file the sprint report. A person approves the checkpoint in the desktop app.

reasoning.rationale: End-to-end interop run that has to follow the orchestrator contract exactly.

tickets.title: Complete a sprint from a second MCP host on the same plan
